evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/components/Toast.tsx:144 — ToastProvider renders only the last MAX_VISIBLE_TOASTS (3) via `visibleToasts = toasts.slice(-MAX_VISIBLE_TOASTS)`, but ALL toasts stay in the `toasts` state array. Error toasts are created with duration = ERROR_DURATION = 0 (lines 68, 78-79), so showToast() (lines 132-138) never schedules an auto-dismiss setTimeout for them. The only removal path for a duration-0 toast is the close button inside ToastItem (line 243) — which is never rendered for a toast that has scrolled out of the visible slice. Consequence: in a session that raises >3 error toasts, the older error toasts are hidden (no close button reachable) AND have no timeout, so they are stuck in `toasts` permanently — unbounded state growth / effective memory leak, and the user can never dismiss them. Fix (frontend-only, cloud-landable): cap the retained array (e.g. drop/auto-expire overflow toasts, or give error toasts a finite max duration), or surface an overflow queue so hidden persistent toasts remain dismissable. Add a Vitest case that pushes 4+ error toasts and asserts the array does not grow unbounded. Medium: UX dead-end + unbounded state, no crash.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/components/ConnectionStatus.tsx:104-113 — the reconnect control is a plain <div> carrying onClick (109), onKeyDown (110) and a conditional tabIndex={!isConnected && !isConnecting ? 0 : -1} (113) while declaring role="status" (111). role="status" is an ARIA live-region role, not an interactive role: a click/keyboard-activated reconnect affordance should expose role="button" (or be a real <button>) so assistive tech announces it as actionable and Enter/Space semantics are conventional. As written, the element doubles as a live region AND a focusable click target only when disconnected, which is inconsistent and also trips Biome's static-interactivity lints (a static element with event handlers). Fix (frontend-only, cloud-landable): render the dot/label as a <button type="button"> (or add role="button") for the reconnect affordance and keep the live-region announcement on a dedicated non-interactive node. Low severity, a11y semantics.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/pages/LoginPage.tsx:80-86 — getErrorMessage() i18n-maps the AuthError codes and a heuristic network case, but its final fallback for any other `error instanceof Error` returns the RAW `error.message` (line 85), which is then rendered as the login error banner (handleSubmit sets errors.general, shown at lines 226-233). On a non-English UI (sk/cs/de) any unmapped thrown Error surfaces untranslated developer/English text on the primary auth surface, and the heuristic `includes('fetch')/('network')` (line 82) is locale/engine-fragile. This is the same raw-backend-message pattern already filed for other surfaces (errorboundary-raw-message-prod, emergency-dir-raw-err-message, signature-modal-raw-err) but is net-new for the login page. Fix (frontend-only, cloud-landable): return a translated generic fallback (t('auth.unexpectedError')) for unmapped errors instead of the raw message, or route it through an error-code catalogue. Low severity, i18n/UX consistency + minor internal-detail disclosure.
